## Three numbers hide the range {#recap}

::: {.two}
::: {}
In Session 1, option A had three payoffs: −120, 80 and 260, with EMV 56.

Real demand is not low, medium or high. It can be any value in a range, and price and cathode cost move too.

Today we replace the three columns with thousands of simulated futures, and ask what the full distribution says about risk.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
Two questions for today. How likely is the new LFP line to lose money? And is it better to build the whole line now, or half now and the rest later?
:::
:::
:::

Question for today: what does the whole distribution of NPV tell us that a single expected value does not?
:::

## Monte Carlo simulation in five steps {#monte-carlo}

::: {.elements}
::: {.el}
[1 · Model]{.label}
Write NPV as a formula of the uncertain inputs.
:::
::: {.el}
[2 · Distributions]{.label}
Give each uncertain input a probability distribution, from data or expert judgment.
:::
::: {.el}
[3 · Sample and repeat]{.label}
Draw one value of every input, compute NPV, and repeat 1,000 or more times.
:::
::: {.el .key}
[4 · Summarize]{.label}
Report the mean, P10, P50, P90 and the probability of loss: the risk profile.
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
Step 5 is to question the result: which input drives the spread, and would a different but reasonable distribution change the decision?
:::

## CellCo's NPV model for option A {#npv-model}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p>NPV = −600 + 6.710 × [ min(2, <i>D</i>) × (<i>P</i> − <i>K</i> − 190) − 35 ]</p></div>
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Input</th><th>Distribution</th><th>Parameters</th><th>Basis</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><i>D</i>, demand for the new capacity, GWh/yr</td><td>Triangular</td><td>min 0.9, most likely 1.7, max 2.5</td><td>sales team's three estimates</td></tr>
    <tr><td><i>P</i>, cell price, CNY/kWh</td><td>Normal</td><td>mean 380, SD 8</td><td>contract history</td></tr>
    <tr><td><i>K</i>, cathode cost, CNY/kWh</td><td>Lognormal</td><td>median 110, log-SD 0.08</td><td>cannot go negative</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Fixed inputs</td><td colspan="3">other variable cost 190 CNY/kWh · fixed cost CNY 35 million/yr · capital cost CNY 600 million · 10 years at 8% (annuity factor 6.710)</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[1 GWh × 1 CNY/kWh = CNY 1 million, so min(2, D) × margin is already in CNY million per year. All values are fictional, written for teaching.]{.note-line}

## In Excel: one row is one future {#excel}

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span><b class="c">F2  U        </b> =RAND()</span><span><b class="c">A2  demand   </b> =IF(F2&lt;0.5, 0.9+SQRT(F2*1.6*0.8), 2.5-SQRT((1-F2)*1.6*0.8))</span><span><b class="c">B2  price    </b> =NORM.INV(RAND(), 380, 8)</span><span><b class="c">C2  cathode  </b> =LOGNORM.INV(RAND(), LN(110), 0.08)</span><span><b class="c">D2  NPV      </b> =-600 + 6.71*(MIN(2,A2)*(B2-C2-190) - 35)</span><span><b class="c">             </b> copy row 2 down to row 1001, then:</span><span><b class="c">summary      </b> =AVERAGE(D2:D1001)   =PERCENTILE.INC(D2:D1001,0.1)   =COUNTIF(D2:D1001,"&lt;0")/1000</span></pre>
```

[The triangular formula is the inverse of its cumulative distribution. (1.7 − 0.9)/(2.5 − 0.9) = 0.5 is the probability that demand falls below the most likely value. Press F9 to draw 1,000 new futures.]{.note-line}

## Run the simulation {#mc-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="mc1"></div>
<script>
window.cellcoMC = function (rootId, opt) {
  const root = document.getElementById(rootId);
  if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const AF10 = 6.7101, AF2 = 1.7833, DF2 = 0.85734, AFL = AF10 - AF2, N = 1000;
  root.innerHTML =
    '<div class="w-controls">' +
      '<span class="w-toggle" role="group" aria-label="Strategy"><button type="button" data-s="commit" aria-pressed="true">Commit now (A)</button><button type="button" data-s="staged" aria-pressed="false">Staged</button></span>' +
      '<label class="w-slider" data-row="T">Expand if demand ≥ <strong data-v="T">1.9</strong><input type="range" data-in="T" min="1.2" max="2.4" step="0.1" value="1.9"></label>' +
      (opt.rho ? '<label class="w-slider">Demand–price correlation <strong data-v="rho">0.0</strong><input type="range" data-in="rho" min="-0.8" max="0.8" step="0.1" value="0"></label>' : '') +
      '<button type="button" class="w-btn" data-run>Run 1,000 futures</button>' +
    '</div>' +
    '<svg viewBox="0 0 1160 250" role="img" aria-label="Histogram of simulated NPV with P10, P50 and P90 marked"></svg>' +
    '<div class="w-readout" aria-live="polite"></div>' +
    (opt.log ? '<div class="mc-log"><table class="wide"><thead><tr><th>Run</th><th>Strategy</th><th class="num">Mean</th><th class="num">P10</th><th class="num">P90</th><th class="num">P(loss)</th><th class="num">CE, R = 100</th><th class="num">CE, R = 400</th></tr></thead><tbody></tbody></table></div>' : '');
  const $ = (s) => root.querySelector(s);
  let strat = 'commit', seed = opt.seed || 11, runNo = 0;
  function rng(a) { return function () { a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0; let t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a); t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t; return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296; }; }
  function erf(x) { const s = Math.sign(x); x = Math.abs(x); const t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * x);
    const y = 1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-x * x); return s * y; }
  const Phi = (z) => 0.5 * (1 + erf(z / Math.SQRT2));
  function simulate() {
    const r = rng(seed), T = +$('[data-in="T"]').value, rho = opt.rho ? +$('[data-in="rho"]').value : 0;
    const gauss = () => { const u = 1 - r(), v = r(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * v); };
    const out = new Float64Array(N);
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
      const z1 = gauss(), z2 = rho * z1 + Math.sqrt(1 - rho * rho) * gauss(), u = Phi(z1);
      const D = u < 0.5 ? 0.9 + Math.sqrt(u * 1.6 * 0.8) : 2.5 - Math.sqrt((1 - u) * 1.6 * 0.8);
      const m = (380 + 8 * z2) - 110 * Math.exp(0.08 * gauss()) - 190;
      if (strat === 'commit') out[i] = -600 + AF10 * (Math.min(2, D) * m - 35);
      else out[i] = -330 + AF2 * (Math.min(1, D) * m - 20) + (D >= T ? -330 * DF2 + AFL * (Math.min(2, D) * m - 35) : AFL * (Math.min(1, D) * m - 20));
    }
    return out;
  }
  const f0 = (x) => Math.round(x).toString().replace('-', '−');
  function draw(x) {
    const s = Array.from(x).sort((a, b) => a - b), q = (p) => s[Math.min(N - 1, Math.floor(p * N))];
    const mean = s.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / N, loss = s.filter((v) => v < 0).length / N;
    const ce = (R) => -R * Math.log(s.reduce((a, v) => a + Math.exp(-v / R), 0) / N);
    const W = 1160, H = 250, L = 50, R = 20, T0 = 10, B = 40, x0 = -500, x1 = 650, bw = 25, nb = (x1 - x0) / bw;
    const X = (v) => L + (v - x0) / (x1 - x0) * (W - L - R), cnt = new Array(nb).fill(0);
    s.forEach((v) => { cnt[Math.max(0, Math.min(nb - 1, Math.floor((v - x0) / bw)))]++; });
    const ymax = Math.max(80, ...cnt), Y = (c) => T0 + (1 - c / ymax) * (H - T0 - B);
    const col = strat === 'commit' ? '#0F6E6B' : '#E29A2D';
    let g = '';
    for (let v = -500; v <= 500; v += 100) g += `<text x="${X(v)}" y="${H - 14}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#333F4A">${String(v).replace('-', '−')}</text>`;
    g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${Y(0)}" y2="${Y(0)}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="${X(0)}" x2="${X(0)}" y1="${T0}" y2="${Y(0)}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/>`;
    cnt.forEach((c, i) => { if (c) g += `<rect x="${X(x0 + i * bw) + 1}" y="${Y(c)}" width="${X(x0 + bw) - X(x0) - 2}" height="${Y(0) - Y(c)}" fill="${col}" opacity=".8"/>`; });
    for (const [p, lab] of [[0.1, 'P10'], [0.5, 'P50'], [0.9, 'P90']]) { const v = q(p); g += `<line x1="${X(v)}" x2="${X(v)}" y1="${T0}" y2="${Y(0)}" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="${X(v) + 5}" y="${T0 + 16}" font-size="15" fill="#1C242B">${lab} ${f0(v)}</text>`; }
    g += `<text x="${W - R}" y="${H - 14}" text-anchor="end" font-size="15" fill="#66727C">NPV, CNY million</text>`;
    $('svg').innerHTML = g;
    const name = strat === 'commit' ? 'Commit now' : `Staged, expand if D ≥ ${(+$('[data-in="T"]').value).toFixed(1)}`;
    $('.w-readout').innerHTML = `<b>${name}</b>: mean <b>${f0(mean)}</b>, P10 ${f0(q(0.1))}, P50 ${f0(q(0.5))}, P90 ${f0(q(0.9))}, ` +
      `P(loss) <span class="best">${Math.round(loss * 100)}%</span>, CE at R = 100: ${f0(ce(100))}, at R = 400: ${f0(ce(400))}. Run ${runNo}, ${N} futures.`;
    if (opt.log) $('.mc-log tbody').insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', `<tr><td>${runNo}</td><td>${name}</td><td class="num">${f0(mean)}</td><td class="num">${f0(q(0.1))}</td><td class="num">${f0(q(0.9))}</td><td class="num">${Math.round(loss * 100)}%</td><td class="num">${f0(ce(100))}</td><td class="num">${f0(ce(400))}</td></tr>`);
  }
  function run() { runNo++; draw(simulate()); seed += 7919; }
  function paint() {
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-s]').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', b.dataset.s === strat));
    $('[data-row="T"]').style.display = strat === 'staged' ? '' : 'none';
    $('[data-v="T"]').textContent = (+$('[data-in="T"]').value).toFixed(1);
    if (opt.rho) $('[data-v="rho"]').textContent = (+$('[data-in="rho"]').value).toFixed(1);
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-s]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => { strat = b.dataset.s; paint(); run(); }));
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-in]').forEach((el) => el.addEventListener('input', paint));
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-in]').forEach((el) => el.addEventListener('change', run));
  $('[data-run]').addEventListener('click', run);
  paint(); run();
};
cellcoMC('mc1', { rho: true, log: false, seed: 11 });
</script>
```

[Each click draws 1,000 new futures, so the numbers move a little every time. That movement is sampling error.]{.hint}

```{=html}
  <thead><tr><th>400,000 runs</th><th class="num">Mean</th><th class="num">P10</th><th class="num">P50</th><th class="num">P90</th><th class="num">P(loss)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Commit now (A)</td><td class="num">57</td><td class="num">−208</td><td class="num">55</td><td class="num">321</td><td class="num hit">40%</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[The mean matches Session 1's EMV of 56, but the simulation shows a 40% chance of loss and a P10 of −208, far below the −120 of the low-demand column. The staged strategy is explained after the break.]{.note-line}

## Activity 1 · Reference values {#act1-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
With 400,000 runs, option A has mean **57**, P10 **−208**, P90 **321** and P(loss) **40%**.

With 1,000 runs, the standard deviation of NPV is about 201, so the standard error of the mean is 201/√1000 ≈ **6.4**. Two honest pairs can differ by about ±13 in the mean.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
Both matter. Fixing price and cathode cost cuts the SD of NPV from 201 to 149; fixing demand at 1.7 cuts it to 136. The margin is small, so its uncertainty is multiplied by the volume and by the annuity factor of 6.7.
:::
:::
:::

## Break · 10 minutes {#break}

::: {.route-question}
After the break: what if CellCo does not have to decide everything today?
:::

## The value of waiting: a real option {#real-option}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Staged strategy.** Build 1 GWh now for CNY 330 million. After two years, CellCo knows its demand. If demand is at least a threshold T, add the second 1 GWh for another CNY 330 million.

Staging costs more in total (660 against 600), and the first two years sell at most 1 GWh. In return, CellCo spends the second 330 only in the futures where it pays.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<div class="formula" style="font-size:.62em"><p>NPV<sub>staged</sub> = −330 + 1.783 × [min(1, <i>D</i>) × <i>m</i> − 20]<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;+ { if <i>D</i> ≥ T: −330 × 0.857 + 4.927 × [min(2, <i>D</i>) × <i>m</i> − 35]<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;otherwise: 4.927 × [min(1, <i>D</i>) × <i>m</i> − 20] }</p></div>
```
[*m* = *P* − *K* − 190. 1.783 is the 2-year annuity factor, 4.927 covers years 3 to 10, and 0.857 discounts year 2.]{.hint}
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
The value of flexibility is E[NPV staged] − E[NPV commit]. A real option is the right, but not the obligation, to invest later.
:::

## Staged against commit {#staged}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>400,000 runs, CNY million</th><th class="num">Mean</th><th class="num">P10</th><th class="num">P90</th><th class="num">P(loss)</th><th class="num">CE, R = 100</th><th class="num">CE, R = 400</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Commit now (A)</td><td class="num">57</td><td class="num">−208</td><td class="num">321</td><td class="num">40%</td><td class="num">−117</td><td class="num">7</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Staged, expand if D ≥ 1.6</td><td class="num">57</td><td class="num">−98</td><td class="num">205</td><td class="num">30%</td><td class="num">−25</td><td class="num">38</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Staged, expand if D ≥ 1.9</td><td class="num hit">79</td><td class="num">−43</td><td class="num">201</td><td class="num">20%</td><td class="num">25</td><td class="num">66</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Staged, expand if D ≥ 2.2</td><td class="num">73</td><td class="num">−35</td><td class="num">179</td><td class="num">19%</td><td class="num hit">35</td><td class="num">64</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
With a threshold of 1.9, staging adds about **22 million** of expected NPV and halves the chance of loss. It gives up some upside: P90 falls from 321 to 201.
:::

## Where simulation misleads {#misleads}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
**Correlated inputs.** We drew price and demand independently. If price falls when demand falls (correlation 0.5), P10 of option A drops from −208 to −239. Ignoring correlation understated the downside.
:::
::: {.tk}
**Chosen distributions.** The triangular range for demand came from three estimates by the sales team. Ask what evidence supports the minimum of 0.9, because the downside depends on it.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
**One draw per input.** The model keeps price and demand fixed for ten years. A model with yearly changes would give a different spread. A simulation is only as good as its model.
:::
:::

[Try the correlation slider on the simulator slide.]{.note-line}

## Tournament · Reference results {#act2-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Threshold T</th><th class="num">Mean</th><th class="num">P(loss)</th><th class="num">CE, R = 100</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>1.6</td><td class="num">57</td><td class="num">30%</td><td class="num">−25</td></tr>
    <tr><td>1.8</td><td class="num">76</td><td class="num">22%</td><td class="num">15</td></tr>
    <tr><td>1.9</td><td class="num hit">79</td><td class="num">20%</td><td class="num">25</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2.0</td><td class="num">77</td><td class="num">20%</td><td class="num">30</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2.2</td><td class="num">73</td><td class="num">19%</td><td class="num">35</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2.4</td><td class="num">71</td><td class="num">19%</td><td class="num hit">37</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
::: {}
A risk-neutral board expands when demand reaches about **1.9 GWh/yr**.

A risk-averse board (R = 100) gains from every increase in T: at **T = 2.4** it almost never expands, and its certainty equivalent is 37. For that board, the 1 GWh line alone is close to the safest choice.

Every staged strategy with T ≥ 1.7 beats committing now on mean, P10 and P(loss).
:::
:::

::: {.bridge}
The best moment to expand depends on the board's risk attitude. A cautious board values the option to wait so highly that it rarely uses the option to expand.
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
Monte Carlo simulation turns a model and input distributions into a full risk profile. Option A's mean NPV of 57 hides a 40% chance of loss.
:::
::: {.tk}
With 1,000 runs, the mean carries a standard error of about 6. Report the run count, and do not read meaning into differences smaller than that.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
Building in stages is a real option. Expanding only if demand reaches 1.9 GWh/yr adds about 22 million of expected NPV and halves the chance of loss.
:::
:::
